Physically outmatched in Combat class and close to being cut from the academy, she is saved when Jiang, the master of Lore, takes her as his apprentice, the first he has accepted in years. Lore is a subject the rest of the faculty regards as worthless. Jiang sets her to meditation, herblore and the old stories of the sixty-four gods, refuses to explain what any of it leads to, and insists that restraint matters more than power. Rin begins to suspect that the gods in those stories are real and reachable, and that Jiang knows exactly how to reach them. Alongside this she studies strategy with Kitay, keeps losing to Nezha, and watches Altan Trengsin, the academy's best student and the last living Speerly, from a distance.

At the academy's end-of-year Tournament, Rin faces Nezha in front of the whole school and the visiting warlords. Losing badly, she reaches for the god Jiang warned her never to touch, and fire answers: she burns Nezha severely and wins the match. Jiang is appalled rather than impressed and tells her that what she has done is not a skill but an opening she may not be able to close. The victory ends her standing as the school's joke and begins her real education, as Jiang finally explains shamanism: the gods can be reached through meditation and drugs, and every shaman pays for the power with their mind. Before the argument between master and student can be settled, the Federation of Mugen, the island empire that has occupied Nikan twice before, attacks. A third Poppy War begins, the academy is emptied, and the students are commissioned and sent to the front.

Rin is assigned not to a regular division but to the Cike, the empire's unit of shamans - assassins the Militia regards as monsters and uses as disposable. Its commander is Altan Trengsin. Its members each answer to a different god: Chaghan, a Hinterlander who can leave his body and steady other shamans' minds; his twin Qara, who sees through birds; Ramsa, a teenage explosives-maker; Baji and Suni, who channel a boar and a monkey and are dangerous to stand beside. Jiang refuses to take any part in the war and disappears, leaving Rin without a teacher and without the control he insisted she needed. The Cike are sent to Khurdalain, a northern port city where the Federation has landed and where the defence is divided between rival Nikara commanders who will not cooperate with one another.

The defence of Khurdalain becomes a grinding stalemate: the city's commanders quarrel, the Federation lands more troops, and the Cike are used for sabotage and assassination rather than open battle. Rin is reunited with Nezha and Kitay, who are serving with a regular division, and the old academy rivalry gives way to something closer to alliance. Rin's fire remains unreliable and she has no one left to teach her; Altan uses her anyway, and she begins to model herself on him - his discipline, his anger, and the opium he uses to reach his god. Chaghan warns her that Altan is not the example she takes him for. The Cike's operations do real damage without changing the shape of the campaign, and the Federation's hold on the coast steadily tightens.

Khurdalain falls. The Federation breaks the city's defences, the feud between the Nikara commanders proves fatal, and the survivors are forced into retreat. In the fighting Nezha is gravely wounded and lost, and Rin believes him dead. The Cike lose members, and Altan's judgement narrows to a single question: how to hurt the Federation badly enough to end the war outright. Orders from the Empress reach him rarely and mean less each time. Rin, who has spent the campaign learning that her god will give her anything the moment she stops resisting it, follows him inland as the unit turns south toward Golyn Niis, the imperial city where the bulk of the Nikara army has fallen back and where Kitay was posted.

The Cike reach Golyn Niis and find that the city has already fallen. The Federation army has killed its population, soldiers and civilians together, on a scale that leaves nothing to defend and nobody to evacuate. Searching the ruins, Rin finds Kitay alive among the dead, physically unhurt and badly damaged by what he witnessed. The atrocity ends any argument within the Cike about restraint. Altan concludes that conventional war is already lost and that the only force left to Nikan is shamanic, and he sets out for the Chuluu Korikh, the stone mountain where shamans who lost themselves to their gods are sealed alive rather than executed, intending to free them and turn them on the Federation. Rin, whose control over what she opened at Sinegard has been slipping all campaign, does not argue with him.

The attempt to raise an army from the Chuluu Korikh fails at once. The first shaman released, Feylen, a former Cike member long since wholly taken over by the wind god, is beyond anyone's command; he escapes into the world as a greater danger than the one he was meant to solve, and the mountain is sealed again with nothing gained. The Cike are scattered, and Altan and Rin are taken by the Federation and shipped to Speer, the burnt island the Federation has used for twenty years as a research station. There Rin learns what was done to the Speerlies who were not killed in the last war, and that Altan was one of the children the Federation's doctors kept and studied. Held, drugged and cut off from her god, she is left with the certainty that nobody is coming for them.

Altan frees Rin and the surviving Cike from the Federation's compound on Speer and stays behind: he calls his god one last time, burns the facility and the researchers in it, and dies in the fire he raises. Rin also learns why Speer was destroyed in the previous war - Empress Su Daji sold the island and its people to the Federation to buy the peace that ended it, and Nikan's rulers have lied about it ever since. Left standing on the ruins of her own people's home, with command of the Cike and nothing restraining her, Rin bargains with the Phoenix and asks it to end the Federation entirely. The god answers: the island nation of Mugen is destroyed and its population, soldiers and civilians together, is killed. The war ends because there is no longer an enemy to fight it. Rin survives what she has done without repenting it, takes command of the Cike, and turns her attention to the Empress who betrayed Speer.

characters.description: The fourth of the nine Loric children, now a fugitive. After the battle in Paradise, Ohio, that killed his guardian Henri, he is on the run with Number Six and his friend Sam Goode, wanted by federal authorities who believe he is a terrorist responsible for destroying a school. His Legacies are still arriving and still unreliable, and he is grieving the only family he had. He wants two things that pull against each other: to find the rest of the nine, and to go back for the girl he left behind in Ohio.
characters.name: John Smith

characters.description: The sixth of the nine Loric children, and the most experienced fighter among the survivors. She can turn invisible, control weather, and think tactically about a war the others are still learning exists. She spent years hunting Mogadorians alone before she found John in Paradise, and she has little patience for his attachments to Earth or for waiting. She takes over John's training and pushes the group toward finding the remaining Garde.
characters.name: Number Six

characters.description: John's human friend from Paradise, who left everything behind to come with him. He has no powers and knows it, but he is the only one of them who grew up reading about this war from the outside, and his father's old research keeps turning out to matter. Loyal past the point of sense, he insists on being part of the fighting rather than being protected from it.
characters.name: Sam Goode

characters.description: The book's second narrator: the seventh of the nine, seventeen years old, living in a convent orphanage in the town of Santa Teresa in northern Spain. She has spent years in a place where nothing happens, untrained and largely unarmed, teaching herself what she can from what the nuns leave lying around. She has quietly developed healing and the ability to breathe underwater, and she scours newspapers and library computers for any report strange enough to be another of her kind. Patient, watchful, and increasingly unwilling to keep waiting for a guardian who has given up.
characters.name: Marina

characters.description: Marina's Cepan, who fled Lorien charged with training and protecting her. Years of hiding wore her down; she took vows at the Santa Teresa convent, embraced her new life as a nun, and now refuses to speak about Lorien, to train Marina, or to say where she hid Marina's Chest. She treats their mission as a delusion best left alone, which leaves Marina effectively alone in a hostile household.
characters.name: Adelina

characters.description: A small girl at the Santa Teresa orphanage who attaches herself to Marina and follows her everywhere. She is sharp, curious, and unafraid of the nuns, and she asks the sort of questions that make Marina careful. She arrived at the convent recently and is the closest thing Marina has to a friend.
characters.name: Ella

characters.description: A man from Santa Teresa who lives with his elderly mother and is known around town mainly for drinking. He befriends Marina, who sees past the local verdict on him, and he proves to be observant, generous, and braver than his reputation. He becomes the only adult in the town Marina can rely on.
characters.name: Hector Ricardo

characters.description: The girl John left behind in Paradise, Ohio. She stood by him after learning what he is, but the manhunt that followed the destruction of the high school has put her under the attention of federal agents. John cannot stop thinking about her, and Six regards any contact with her as an unacceptable risk.
characters.name: Sarah Hart

characters.description: The Chimaera who has guarded John since Lorien, most often in the shape of a beagle. He travels with the group, changes form as the situation requires, and communicates with John directly. He is treated as a member of the team rather than a pet.
characters.name: Bernie Kosar

characters.description: Sam's father, who vanished from Paradise years before after becoming convinced that visitors from another world had come to Earth. He left behind a hidden collection of research, maps, and notes that Sam never knew existed. What he was actually working on turns out to be accurate, and it gives the group the first solid lead they have ever had on the enemy's operations.
characters.name: Malcolm Goode

characters.description: The ninth of the nine Loric children, held prisoner deep inside a Mogadorian mountain base. He has survived captivity by being harder than his captors, and he is loud, reckless, and physically the strongest of the Garde met so far, with the ability to move along walls and ceilings as though gravity had no claim on him. His Cepan, Sandor, did not survive the capture.
characters.name: Number Nine

characters.description: The Cepan who arrives in Spain for Marina and Ella. He came to Earth on a second Loric ship, later than the first, and he carries the part of Lorien's history that the nine were never told. He is calm, prepared, and clearly has been searching for a long time.
characters.name: Crayton

recaps.ending: In West Virginia, John and Sam fight their way into the Mogadorian mountain base and find Number Nine, who has been held prisoner there since his own capture, and free him. Getting out costs them: Sam is taken by the Mogadorians, and John, out of options, has to leave without him. John, Nine, and Bernie Kosar escape, and John's first commitment afterward is to get Sam back. In Spain, the Mogadorians move on Santa Teresa in force. Hector Ricardo dies helping Marina and Ella get clear, and Adelina, who spent years refusing the fight, is killed defending Marina. Number Six arrives in time to turn the battle, and Ella reveals that she is Number Ten, a Garde who came to Earth on a second Loric ship that arrived after the first. Her Cepan, Crayton, comes for her, and he can explain the second ship, the war on Lorien, and how much of the history the nine were never told. Marina, Ella, Six, and Crayton leave Spain together. Two groups of Garde now exist instead of scattered individuals, both of them looking for the others, and the Mogadorians hold Sam as leverage.
recaps.in_short: The story splits between two of the nine. John Smith is a fugitive, hunted as a terrorist after the battle in Paradise, moving through the American south with Number Six and Sam Goode while Six trains him. In Spain, Number Seven, called Marina, has spent years in a convent orphanage in Santa Teresa with her Cepan Adelina, who abandoned the mission, became a nun, and will not train her or return her Chest. Marina hunts the news for other Garde, protects a young orphan named Ella, and befriends a local man, Hector Ricardo. John's group returns to Paradise, where John is caught by federal agents and freed by Six, and where Sam's missing father's hidden research points them to a Mogadorian base in West Virginia. Six leaves to find the other Garde while John and Sam go into the mountain. Mogadorians attack Santa Teresa: Hector and Adelina die, Six arrives, Ella is revealed to be Number Ten from a second Loric ship, and her Cepan Crayton collects them. John frees Number Nine from the mountain base, but Sam is captured.

recaps.text: Nine gifted Loric children were evacuated to Earth with adult guardians called Cepans when the Mogadorians destroyed the planet Lorien. A charm placed on the nine means they can be killed only in the order of their numbers, and only while they are apart. Numbers One, Two, and Three were tracked down and killed one by one, the last of them in Kenya. Number Four grew up on the run as John Smith and settled with his guardian Henri in Paradise, Ohio, where he went to high school, fell for Sarah Hart, befriended Sam Goode, and adopted a stray beagle he named Bernie Kosar. His Legacies arrived: light and fire in his hands, then telekinesis, then the ability to reach animals. The Mogadorians traced him to Paradise and attacked the high school. Number Six, the most experienced of the surviving Garde, arrived mid-battle, and Bernie Kosar revealed himself as a Chimaera, a Loric shape-shifter sent to guard John. They destroyed the enemy force, but Henri was killed. John left Paradise with Six, Sam, and Bernie Kosar to find the remaining Garde, leaving Sarah behind. Three of the nine are dead; six are alive and scattered.

John, Six, and Sam are living out of motels in the American south under false names. The destruction of the Paradise high school has been blamed on John, whose face is on the news as a wanted terrorist, and the manhunt makes ordinary movement dangerous. Six trains John hard, pushing him toward control rather than raw force, and pushes the group toward the only strategy she believes in: finding the rest of the nine before the Mogadorians do. In northern Spain, the seventh of the nine has been waiting instead. Known as Marina, she lives in a convent orphanage in the town of Santa Teresa with her Cepan Adelina, who long ago gave up the mission, took vows as a nun, hid Marina's Chest, and refuses to speak about Lorien at all. Marina has taught herself what she can and has already found that she can heal injuries and breathe underwater. She reads every strange story she can reach on the convent's computers, looking for evidence that another of her kind is alive.

Marina's life at the convent narrows to two allies: Ella, a small, sharp orphan girl who follows her everywhere, and Hector Ricardo, a man from the town whom Santa Teresa has written off as a drunk and who turns out to be neither stupid nor a coward. Adelina, meanwhile, treats Marina's insistence on the mission as a danger to them both. Marina finds the American news reports about the school in Ohio and is certain they describe a Garde. In the United States, John's group goes back to Paradise despite the risk: John needs to see Sarah, and Sam wants his father's things. In Sam's house they find a hidden basement full of the research Sam's father assembled before he disappeared, including maps of sites he believed the visitors and their enemies used.

Returning to Paradise costs John. Federal agents are waiting for him and he is taken into custody, and Six gets him out, which leaves him with a doubt about Sarah that he cannot settle and will not say aloud. The research from Sam's father's basement gives them a target: a site in the mountains of West Virginia that his notes mark as important. In Spain, strangers begin appearing in Santa Teresa asking questions that have nothing to do with the town, and Marina, whose Legacies now include seeing in the dark, understands what they are. Adelina refuses to run and refuses to arm her, so Marina prepares alone, trying to get Ella out of danger without explaining what the danger is.

The group splits. Six leaves John and Sam in order to search for the other Garde on her own terms, arguing that spreading out finds them faster. John and Sam head for the West Virginia site with Bernie Kosar, following Sam's father's notes toward a mountain that on paper is nothing at all. In Santa Teresa the strangers stop pretending to be anything else, and the convent stops being a place Marina can hide in. Adelina still refuses to run, to arm her, or to say where she put the Chest, and the nuns are no help. Marina prepares alone, with Hector Ricardo the only adult in the town willing to believe her, and tries to get Ella somewhere safe without being able to explain what the danger actually is.

John and Sam get inside the West Virginia mountain and find a full Mogadorian base cut into the rock, with tunnels, laboratories, beasts, and cells. They learn that the enemy's presence on Earth is far larger and far older than anything Henri described, and that prisoners are being kept alive there for reasons nobody explains. In Spain the Mogadorians attack Santa Teresa openly. Marina, Ella, and Hector are driven out of the convent and through the town in a running fight, Marina finally has her Chest and no time to learn what is in it, and Adelina, cornered with them, has to choose between the life she built as a nun and the one she abandoned. Marina, who spent the whole book asking to be trained, is fighting a war she was never prepared for with a child to protect.

The battle at Santa Teresa costs Marina both of the people who stood with her: Hector Ricardo dies buying her and Ella time to get clear, and Adelina, who spent years insisting the mission was a delusion, is killed defending Marina from the soldiers sent for her. Number Six reaches Spain and turns the fight, and in its aftermath Ella reveals that she is Number Ten: a Garde who came to Earth on a second Loric ship that landed later than the first, a ship the nine were never told about. Her Cepan, Crayton, arrives for her and can explain the rest of Lorien's fall. Marina, Ella, Six, and Crayton leave Spain together. In West Virginia, John and Sam find Number Nine held prisoner in the Mogadorian base and free him, but the escape goes wrong and Sam is captured; John has to leave him behind. John, Nine, and Bernie Kosar get out. The survivors are now in two groups instead of scattered individuals, each hunting for the other, and the Mogadorians hold a hostage John intends to recover.
